issues.description: SQL Injection vulnerability in searchTodos function. The function concatenates user input directly into SQL queries using template literals without parameterized statements.
issues.suggestion: Replace string concatenation with parameterized queries. Use: db.query('SELECT * FROM todos WHERE title LIKE $1 OR description LIKE $2', [`%${keyword}%`, `%${keyword}%`])

issues.description: SQL Injection vulnerability in searchTodosByStatus function. User input is directly concatenated into SQL query without validation or parameterization.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized queries with bound parameters: db.query('SELECT * FROM todos WHERE completed = $1', [completed])

issues.description: SQL Injection vulnerability in getTodosByUser function. User ID is interpolated directly into SQL query using template literals without any input sanitization.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized queries: db.query('SELECT t.* FROM todos t JOIN user_todos ut ON t.id = ut.todo_id WHERE ut.user_id = $1', [userId])

issues.description: Inconsistent error handling between secure functions (createTodo, getTodoById) and vulnerable search functions. Search functions lack try-catch blocks and proper error handling.
issues.suggestion: Implement consistent error handling across all functions. Wrap database operations in try-catch blocks and return appropriate error responses.

issues.description: No input validation for search parameters. The search functions don't validate or sanitize input before using it in queries.
issues.suggestion: Add input validation before query execution: check string length, type, and implement schema validation using zod or joi.

issues.description: Inconsistent query patterns between secure functions (createTodo using parameterized queries) and vulnerable functions (search functions using string interpolation).
issues.suggestion: Standardize all database queries to use parameterized queries exclusively. Create a query builder utility for consistency.

issues.description: No query result limits on search functions. searchTodos and searchTodosByStatus could return large datasets without pagination, causing performance issues.
issues.suggestion: Implement pagination with LIMIT and OFFSET clauses. Add optional parameters for page size and offset.

issues.description: Missing logging for search operations. Unlike critical operations like createTodo, search functions lack audit logging for compliance and debugging.
issues.suggestion: Add structured logging for all database operations using a logger. Log query parameters (non-sensitive), execution time, and result count.

issues.description: Lack of TypeScript type safety for query results. Search functions return loosely-typed results.
issues.suggestion: Define TypeScript interfaces for all return types and ensure strict type safety throughout.

issues.description: No database indexes consideration for search queries. Queries on title or status fields may perform full table scans.
issues.suggestion: Ensure database indexes exist on frequently searched columns (title, status, userId). Document required indexes.

codeQuality.summary: CRITICAL: The src/todo.ts file contains three CRITICAL SQL injection vulnerabilities in the newly added search functions (searchTodos, searchTodosByStatus, getTodosByUser). These functions concatenate user input directly into SQL queries using template literals and string concatenation, creating severe security risks. The rest of the codebase demonstrates good security practices with parameterized queries (see createTodo, getTodoById), making these vulnerabilities stand out as dangerous inconsistencies. Additional issues include: missing error handling, no input validation, lack of pagination, missing audit logging, and performance concerns. The overall code quality score is 28/100 - immediate remediation required before this PR can be merged.

suggestions.description: The three search functions follow nearly identical patterns: accept a parameter, construct a SQL query, execute it, and return results as Todo[]. This repetition violates DRY principle.
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates code duplication across search functions, centralizes parameterized query execution, makes adding new search functions consistent and easier, reduces maintenance burden, improves testability by creating a single queryTodos function to mock, and ensures all queries use parameterized statements for security.

suggestions.description: All three search functions use unsafe string concatenation/interpolation instead of parameterized queries. This is a critical security anti-pattern that contradicts the secure pattern used in createTodo and getTodoById.
suggestions.benefits: Prevents SQL injection attacks by using parameterized queries, adds input validation and length checks, implements proper error handling with try-catch, maintains consistency with secure functions like createTodo, provides clear security model, and follows database driver best practices.

suggestions.description: The sanitizeInput function is well-implemented but uses repetitive replace calls. Could be simplified using a utility object or array of replacements.
suggestions.benefits: Simplifies code by using a single regex replace with lookup table, improves performance with fewer passes through the string, makes the entity mapping more maintainable and easier to extend, reduces code lines while improving readability.

suggestions.description: The export interfaces are well-defined. Could add JSDoc comments for better IDE support and documentation.
suggestions.benefits: Adds comprehensive JSDoc documentation for better IDE autocomplete and type hints, improves code discoverability and maintainability, provides clear contract for developers using these types, helps with automated documentation generation tools.

refactorings.summary: The src/todo.ts file contains high-impact refactoring opportunities, primarily focused on eliminating code duplication and fixing security anti-patterns. The three search functions share nearly identical structure and all use unsafe string concatenation instead of parameterized queries. High-priority refactoring: Extract a common queryTodos utility function to eliminate duplication and ensure consistent use of parameterized queries. This single refactoring would address both the DRY principle violation and the critical SQL injection vulnerabilities. Medium-priority: Simplify sanitizeInput using a more elegant pattern. Low-priority: Add JSDoc documentation to interfaces. Implementing these refactorings would improve code maintainability, eliminate duplicated logic, and most importantly, fix the critical security vulnerabilities in the search functions.

recommendations.description: Fix SQL injection vulnerabilities in all three search functions (searchTodos, searchTodosByStatus, getTodosByUser). Replace string concatenation/interpolation with parameterized queries using bound parameters ($1, $2, etc.). This is the most critical issue preventing PR merge.

Create comprehensive test coverage for all functions in src/todo.ts, with special focus on security testing for the three vulnerable search functions. Test for SQL injection prevention, input validation, and edge cases. Zero test coverage currently exists.
Add input validation to all search functions before query execution. Validate string length, type, and implement schema validation for type safety. Functions currently accept unvalidated user input.
Implement consistent error handling across all functions. Add try-catch blocks to database operations in search functions to match the error handling pattern used in createTodo and getTodoById.

Eliminate code duplication by extracting a common queryTodos utility function. The three search functions follow identical patterns and can be consolidated. This will improve maintainability and ensure consistent use of secure query patterns.
